children: The executive responsible for JPMorgan Chase's vast credit card business, among the largest in the world, is leaving the bank, according to an internal memo viewed by Barron's.
Allison Beer, the CEO of card and connected commerce, "has informed me of her decision to leave the firm for an external opportunity," JPMorgan Co-President Troy Rohrbaugh said in a memo on Friday.
"She and her team have played an important part in moving our card business to where it is today," he said in the memo to employees.
Beer's exit is notable because she is among the most powerful leaders in the credit card industry.

JPMorgan's card business is among the world's largest by customer spending and balances. She is leaving for another company at a moment when banks are competing fiercely with each other to win over cardholders with perks, especially spenders who are higher earners.
Rohrbaugh's team plans to name a new leader for the card and connected commerce businesses in the coming weeks, he wrote. In the meantime, those who reported to Beer will report to Rohrbaugh.
A JPMorgan spokesman declined to specify who will replace Beer. Beer didn't immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

Beer joined JPMorgan as a top payments executive from American Express in. 2017. She has been a key executive on the leadership team led by Rohrbaugh, who was promoted in June to JPMorgan co-president and leader of the sprawling consumer- and community-banking business.

Earlier this year, Beer's team announced the bank would take over the Apple Card program from Goldman Sachs. The deal to become the card's issuer expanded JPMorgan's already-dominant position in the credit card space.
Beer's earlier roles in JPMorgan's consumer-banking arm included chief product officer and head of corporate development for banking and payments.
